newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy babysitter will not seek investigation.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy babysitter will not seek investigation.

text.p: The family of a teenage babysitter who reportedly had an affair with the son of the late Robert Kennedy said on Tuesday it would not pursue a criminal investigation.
The Boston Globe reported on April 25 that, according to unnamed sources, Michael Kennedy, 39, and the girl -- now 19 -- had a relationship that started when she was 14 and ended last fall.
Robert Kennedy, who was assassinated in 1968, was the brother of President John F. Kennedy. He served in his brother's adminstration as attorney general and was senator from New York.
Based on the Globe story, the Norfolk County District Attorney began that day a "preliminary review" of the allegations. Sex with a minor under the age of 16 is a criminal offence in Massachusetts.

"We have no interest in pursuing any prosecution because it would not be in the girl's interest to do so," the family's lawyer Robert Popeo told Reuters. "To subject her to the long media barrage certainly would not be in her best mental health."

The girl, identified only as the daughter of June and Paul Verrochi, chairman of American Medical Response and a close friend of the Kennedy family, broke off the relationship last fall before she entered college, the Globe said.
"It's up to the district attorney to take action," Popeo said. "They (the family) are not filing any criminal complaint or seeking to institute any criminal action."
Without the testimony of the girl it would be difficult for the district attorney to pursue charges.
The District Attorney's office did not return phone calls seeking comment.
Calls to Kennedy's office and his lawyer, Thomas Dwyer, were also not returned. At the time the story broke, Dwyer said the matter was under "legal review" and he had no comment to make.
The controversy around Michael Kennedy, head of the non-profit Citizens Energy Corp., has damaged the political hopes of his brother, Representative Joseph Kennedy.
The Democratic Congressman, who is preparing to run for governor of Massachusetts, suffered in opinion polls following news of his brother's alleged relationship.

Just weeks ago considered the top Democratic candidate and the only challenger to Republican Gov. William Weld, Representative Kennedy is now in a tight race with hopefuls from both parties after the withdrawal of Weld, according to polls.
